title: Music Therapy in Post-Stroke Patients: A Clinical Trial
official: Effects of Music Therapy on Sleep Quality in Post-Stroke Patients: A Clinical Trial at the San Cecilio University Hospital
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if music therapy works to optimizate sleep quality in patients who have suffered a stroke. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the effect of music therapy on subjective sleep quality in stroke patients?
* What is the effect of music therapy on the subjective perception of insomnia in stroke patients?
* What is the effect of music therapy on levels of hospital anxiety and depression in stroke patients?
* What is the level of satisfaction with the music therapy intervention?

Researchers will compare an intervention group consisting of patients who will undergo music therapy with a control group of participants receiving standard care without music therapy sessions.

Participants will:

* Complete some questionaries about sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), inmsonia (Insomnia Severity Index), anxiety and depression associated with hospitalization (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale) before and after de intervention.
* Intervention group receive daily 60-minute music therapy sessions at night during their hospitalization, whenever possible.
* Intervention gruop have to report their perceived level of satisfaction with the music therapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis or suspected diagnosis of stroke.
* Admission to the Neurology Department of the Hospital Universitario Clínico San Cecilio (HUCSC).
* Score ≥ 5 on the Canadian Neurological Scale.
* Preserved cognitive function.
* Glasgow Coma Scale score ≥ 14.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Language impairment (aphasia).
* Significant difficulties understanding the language.
* Cognitive impairments affecting comprehension.
* Acute psychiatric disorders and/or states of agitation.
* Severe hearing impairment or profound deafness.
* Diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea.
* Restless legs syndrome.
* Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
* Narcolepsy.
